text: Every school year, new students, transferees,
and visitors walk through the gates of Notre Dame of Marbel University.
It's a big campus, full of buildings, offices, and places to discover.
But finding your way isn't always easy.
Most newcomers have to ask around, or rely on signs.
So our study set out to build three things: an augmented reality campus tour,
AR assisted navigation, and one place for campus information.
Meet ExploreNDMU.
An Android app built with Unity, AR Foundation, and ARCore.
It works fully offline, and it greets you with a quick tour of what it can do.
Looking for an office?
Open the directory.
Search, or browse by category, and read each place's details and services.
Save the places you visit often, so they're always one tap away.
Now, let's go to the Library.
Tap Navigate here, and choose where you're starting from.
Then, lift your phone.
Gold arrows appear on the ground through your camera, showing the way,
step by step.
A voice tells you when to turn,
and the screen shows how far you have left to go.
No map reading.
No need to ask for directions.
Just follow the arrows.
When you arrive, a gold pin marks your destination,
and an info card tells you about the place in front of you.
New to campus?
Start a guided tour from any of the four gates.
The app leads you from stop to stop, and you can skip a stop whenever you like.
Scan a printed marker, and the university's statues appear in 3D.
Mother Mary, Saint Marcellin Champagnat, and the Bronze Stallion.
Walk around them, and see every detail up close.
How does it work?
Our team walked the campus routes and recorded them.
The app joins these paths,
and uses Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm to
find the best way to your destination.
Everything lives inside the app, so newcomers can find their way,
get information in one place, and reach where they're going,
without asking for directions.
ExploreNDMU.
Your campus, in your hands.
Explore.
Navigate.
Discover.
